coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 45 files, 8 units (the domain directory itself plus 03.01, 03.02, 03.03, 03.04, 03.05, 03.06, 03.08). Matches the expected 8 units / 45 files exactly. 03.07, 03.09, 03.10 and 03.11 are flat feature files living in the domain-root unit; 03.06.01, 03.06.04, 03.04.01 and 03.01.01 are [DEEP] files of 200-290 lines each and were read in full in chunks. All 45 files were read line-by-line in full; no sampling. Zero broken relative links across the domain (verified programmatically). Dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A for every unit: they are owned by meta/problem-statement.md, meta/constraints.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, and every unit here references rather than redefines them (the tree's own rule: 'NEVER redefine a persona here - reference only'). Dimensions 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 were scored for every unit.

findings.claim: Silent contradiction: the graph's freshness rule makes an edge traversable 60 seconds after mutual confirmation of a credit, while the edge-source table and D-07 make traversability conditional on the credit being PUBLIC. Confirmed and public are distinct states in domain 02 (embargo), so the two rules give opposite answers for a confirmed-but-embargoed credit, with no marker on either.
findings.evidence: 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:74 'An edge becomes traversable **within 60 seconds** of the pair's mutual confirmation in domain 02.' | 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:111 (Performance requirements table) '| Derivation -> edge traversable | **< 60 s** | A credit confirmed on the day should path on the day |' | CONTRADICTED BY 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:55 (Edge sources table, Session attestation row) 'Citable: Yes, **once the credit is public**' | 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:229 'D-07 | **Citability is a precondition of traversability** - if we cannot show why, we cannot use it'. The embargo state is real and is flagged elsewhere in this very domain: community-networking-cx.md:372 'A leak-with-a-fuse: must not become visible before the credit publishes (02.01.05 embargo).' The file itself uses the same public/non-public gate for domain 07 rows (line 60 'Yes, once released'; line 62 'Excluded until release'), proving the distinction is deliberate elsewhere.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether a confirmed-but-unpublished credit produces a traversable edge. Choosing the 60-second rule leaks the existence of an unannounced collaboration through path evidence; choosing D-07 breaks the stated <60s derivation budget for every embargoed credit. Nothing in the file, its Open Questions (Q-01 through Q-05), or the parent index states which wins.

findings.claim: 03.04.04 records the fail-open/fail-closed question as unresolved in both its States table and its Q-04, while 03.04.01 D-03 has already ratified the answer (fail closed) and names 03.04.04 explicitly as bound by it. A decided rule is presented as an open fork in the feature that consumes it.

CONTRADICTED BY 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:225 'D-03 | Traversal failure degrades to **`unknown`**, never to `"no path"` | ... **All consumers fail closed on `unknown`**.' and 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:169 'Consumers must fail closed on `unknown`: 03.04.02 must not broker on it, **03.04.04 must not decide reachability on it**' and 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:210 'Reachability must fail closed on `unknown` (D-03), which sharpens its own Q-04.' Also community-networking-cx.md:349 'If the reachability check is unavailable, results fail *closed* (hidden), never shown-and-broken.'
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer reading 03.04.04's own States table implements an undefined error branch (or waits for /create-prd-architecture); one reading 03.04.01 D-03 implements fail-closed. Q-04 as written states no residue beyond the binary that D-03 already answers, so the tracking is not a narrowing - it is a duplicate of a settled decision, in the opposite direction.

findings.claim: The reachability policy ladder parameterises a level by 'N hops' and states only a default for N, never its permitted range. Any N > 2 is unanswerable because 03.04.01 D-05 caps traversal at 2 hops absolutely, and no tracked question covers N's domain.
findings.evidence: 03.04.04-reachability-inbound-policy.md:44 '| **Within N hops** | a path of <= N edges connects you (default N = 2) | shortest-path <= N on the collaboration graph (03.04.01) |'. The word 'default' implies N is user-settable. CONTRADICTED BY 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:227 'D-05 | **Depth limit is 2 hops.** Beyond 2: `"no path within intro range"` ... At 2 hops one human knows both ends and can vouch; at 3 nobody can'. 03.04.04's Q-01 (line 126) covers only 'What is the default' rung of the ladder, not the range of N; Q-02, Q-03 and Q-04 cover the marketplace exemption, disclosure and error behaviour respectively.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the allowed value set for N. Permitting N=3 silently requires a 3-hop traversal that D-05 forbids the graph to answer; restricting N to {1,2} makes 'Within N hops' at N=1 indistinguishable from the adjacent 'Evidenced only' rung, collapsing a 5-level ladder to 4.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file states that accepting a connection MAY auto-create a mutual follow, while 03.01.01 D-12 ratifies that it must not. The feature file records that the CX file needed reconciling; the domain-level CX was updated (R-07) but this sub-domain CX was not, leaving an affirmative 'MAY' against a ratified prohibition.
findings.evidence: 03.01-connections-follows-endorsements-cx.md:58 (CX-02 synthesis 2) 'Accepting a connection MAY auto-create a mutual follow - a convenience most networks implement. If it does, unfollowing later must not silently sever the connection. `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`.' CONTRADICTED BY 03.01.01-follows.md:180 'D-12 | **No auto-follow on connection accept** | DT-11. The reconciliation landed only at domain level: community-networking-cx.md:387 'R-07 | ... Considered auto-following on connection *accept* - the LinkedIn default. Rejected per 03.01.01 DT-11/D-12'.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer working from the sub-domain CX file treats auto-follow-on-accept as an open convenience option and may build it, silently inflating follower counts - the exact metric 03.01.01 DT-06 establishes as booking currency that must stay honest.

No marker sits on either statement.

findings.claim: The behaviour for an entrant withdrawing after judging has begun is marked with a bare `[PENDING]` carrying neither owner nor deferral stage, and no Open Question in the file or its parent covers withdrawal.
findings.evidence: 03.08.02-submissions-eligibility.md:57 '| Entrant withdraws after judging starts | Judges have already spent time; other entrants may be affected | `[PENDING]` |'. The file's Open Questions are Q-01 (does a contest generate a credit), Q-02 (excluding established professionals), Q-03 (sample clearance) - none covers withdrawal. The parent's questions are Q-01 (boundary with domain 21), Q-02 (resolved), Q-03 (credit), Q-04 (entry fee) - none covers it either. The sibling file tracks the structurally identical gap properly: 03.08.03-judging-voting-anti-gaming.md:113 'Q-04 | What is the fallback when a judge goes silent? ... A missing transition on an otherwise complete state machine is an interaction-spec gap for this shard | Agent | `/write-architecture-spec`', and its States table entry (line 76) points at that owned question.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether a withdrawn entry is removed from the judged set mid-judging, scored anyway, or blocks withdrawal after the Frozen transition - and whether the withdrawn entrant's rights position reverts under 03.08.04 D-05 or remains bound by the frozen brief terms they accepted at submission.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX defers its only structural open question (do native posts and work-events share one stream or occupy separate surfaces) to two targets that do not exist: a 'Q-01 on this file' in a CX file that has no Open Questions section, and 'the parent's Q-01', which is a different and already-resolved question about one-feed coherence.
findings.evidence: 03.02-activity-feed-ranking-cx.md:12 (CX-03 map row) 'Unresolved whether posts and work-events share a stream or occupy separate surfaces - **see the parent's Q-01**' | 03.02-activity-feed-ranking-cx.md:72 'CX-03 ... `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` - Medium confidence, and the open question is structural: do posts and work-events share one stream, or are they separate surfaces? ... which is an argument for not building it (**Q-01 on this file**).' The CX file contains no Open Questions section (verified: it runs Cross-Cut Map -> Cross-Cut Details -> Rejected Pairs -> Related Specs). The parent's Q-01 is 03.02-activity-feed-ranking-index.md:68 '~~Is one feed serving a session drummer and a fan actually coherent (D-03)?~~ **RESOLVED - yes, one feed; D-03 stands.**' - a different question, already closed. findings.forcedInvention: The only tracking for whether the post surface is a separate stream points at nothing, so the question has no owner and no stage. An implementer must either treat 03.02.03's shared-stream statement as authoritative (contradicting the CX's 'unresolved') or invent a separate-surface design.

findings.claim: 03.03.04 D-03 makes calls expire and defines an Expired state gated on 'the horizon', but no horizon value is stated and no Open Question tracks it - while the two structurally identical lifecycle parameters elsewhere in the domain are both explicitly tracked to an owner and a stage.

The file's Open Questions are Q-01 (is this domain 04's feature), Q-02 (push or pull), Q-03 (high-response triage), Q-04 (unused speculative submissions) - none names the horizon. CONTRAST the sibling parameters, both tracked: 03.03.03-open-to-status-availability-signals.md:117 'Q-01 | What is the expiry horizon (DT-01)? ... The unit of decision is a per-appetite-type TTL driving the `Expiring` -> `Lapsed` transition | User | `/write-be-spec`' and 03.01.02-professional-connections.md:127 'Q-05 | ... What is the expiry horizon on an unanswered inbound connection request? ... no period is stated here or anywhere in the tree, **and it is not a free parameter** ... | User | `/write-be-spec`'.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the call expiry period. The tree's own treatment of the two analogous horizons establishes that this class of parameter is not free (it trades the ghost-call failure against destroying a slow poster's genuine search), yet here it is neither valued nor owned.
